scope: All 16 retained genuine Astra ToolHang episodes: two pilots and all scheduled outcomes from three completed mechanism batches. Fixed-command verification runs are excluded because they are not independent policy decisions. Removed episodes are excluded. Microwave pilot is discussed separately because task and initial-settling protocol differ.
limitations: Retrospective coding by one reviewer; categories are descriptive and not independently validated causal labels.
Episodes share starts within studies and differ in protocols across studies; pooled counts are not success-rate estimates or independent statistical samples.
First incident means first unsuccessful manipulation or cancelled approach, not first numerical pose residual; cancelled approaches are execution events, not failed grasps.
Terminal stage identifies the unresolved physical problem, not its unique underlying cause. A correct failure acknowledgment is not task success.

Overstated completion means an unqualified full-success finish disagrees with the frozen native scorer. Visible suspension can still be real, and exact native tolerances need not be observable from public images.
Returned reasons are self-reports, not complete internal reasoning or proof that a stated belief caused a decision.
Source hashes in results.json support reproducibility; source changes require reviewing classifications again rather than silently accepting regenerated counts.

episodes.note: First close reaches its selected height but acquires nothing; lower retry succeeds. Blocked insertion and withdrawal recover. Original instruction did not explicitly specify larger hole.
Frame placement is recovered; tool falls after release despite apparent threading. Final retry exhausts motion budget.
Final tool is genuinely released and suspended by correct larger hole, but shallow/off-axis engagement fails native tolerances. Distinguish physical suspension from full benchmark success.
Later first executed frame grasp is empty and recovers. Tool passes; frame remains unseated despite upright-support finish.
Frame assembly initially passes. Joint-limited tool reorientation and whole-arm recovery collision destroy assembly; model acknowledges failure.
Recovered frame slip; shallow insertion and snagged withdrawal. Terminal smaller hole is on hook despite larger-hole descriptions; frame never assembles.
Reached insertion targets do not establish full depth; withdrawal pulls frame out and later recovery misses. No tool-hanging attempt is completed.
Measured corrections leave shaft beside socket. Apparent hole-hook overlap fails threading; tool remains on hand and falls. Overall failure judgment is correct despite optimistic frame subclaim.

Frame assembly recovers. Arm reconfiguration and later tool placement fail. Finish explicitly reports occluded seating uncertainty; do not count as unqualified false success. First-pair prompt mismatch limits attribution.
Model detects near-empty close without interrupt and retries; remeasures held rod; contact correction succeeds. First-pair prompt mismatch prevents mechanism attribution.
Both empty interruptions lead to model-selected recoveries. First tool release falls; model notices and changes placement strategy before verified success.
Recovered frame slip; final reached tool targets contact wrong frame section/table. Finish describes larger-hole hanging with experimental budget still available.
Empty frame close recovers. Blocked crossing leads to higher route. Fresh hook/ring measurements precede successful release and settling.
Frame release fails then overhead observation/regrasp recovers assembly. Final tool rests on base. Rejected 205-step request costs a decision; no finish claim before budget exhaustion.

Initial grasp succeeds. Open hand carries frame through withdrawal; retries never establish seating. Final tool truly hangs by correct hole but shallow/off-axis geometry and frame seating fail native checks.
Two empty attempts recover after changing grasp orientation. Contact-limited seating and withdrawal persist; tool falls and recovery catches stand shaft. Finish accurately acknowledges failure.
